integrations.providers.channel_gmail.cre: Google Cloud Console -> APIs & Services -> Credentials -> OAuth 2.0 Client ID. Configure Authorized Redirect URI to <yourdomain>/api/communication_channels/oauth/gmail/callback.
Paired with the Client ID above. Stored encrypted at rest.
Defaults to gmail.modify + userinfo.email which is enough for send + receive + label management. Leave blank to use defaults.
integrations.providers.channel_gmail.des: Connect per-user Gmail accounts via OAuth2. Outbound via gmail.users.messages.send; inbound via History API polling (5-min default).
integrations.providers.channel_imap.cred: Address used as the From header when sending. Must be deliverable by the SMTP server.
Hostname of the IMAP server. Typically the same hostname your mail client uses.
Use a per-app password if your provider offers one. Stored encrypted at rest.
Prefer implicit TLS. STARTTLS is acceptable. None disables encryption and should only be used inside a private network for testing.
Often the same as the IMAP password; provider-dependent.
integrations.providers.channel_imap.desc: Connect any IMAP-capable mailbox (Fastmail, Proton Bridge, generic IMAP host) for inbound polling and outbound SMTP send.
integrations.providers.gateway_stripe.cr: Stripe Dashboard -> Developers -> API keys. Copy the Publishable key for the same mode you use here (test or live).
Stripe Dashboard -> Developers -> API keys. Use the Secret key from the same mode. In live mode Stripe may only show it once, so reveal or rotate it there if needed.
Use the Stripe endpoint signing secret that starts with whsec_, not your API key.
integrations.providers.gateway_stripe.de: Accept card payments, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and bank transfers via Stripe.
integrations.providers.gateway_stripe.we: For local development, expose your app through a public HTTPS tunnel and use that public URL in Stripe.
Set the destination URL to your public Helios URL plus /api/payment_gateways/webhook/stripe.
Subscribe to the payment and dispute events listed below.
Create or open your Stripe webhook endpoint in Workbench.
Save the Stripe integration credentials, then test the payment flow again.
Reveal the endpoint signing secret and paste the whsec_... value into the Webhook Signing Secret field in Integrations.
Configure a Stripe webhook endpoint so payment status changes, refunds, failed payments, and disputes stay synchronized with Helios.
integrations.providers.storage_s3.creden: AWS IAM access key ID, or the equivalent key for your S3-compatible provider.
Choose how the AWS SDK should authenticate. For production deployments, prefer IAM roles (IRSA/instance profile) when available.
Credentials provided by AWS (STS / IRSA / instance profile)
The S3 bucket where files will be stored.
Custom S3 endpoint URL. Leave empty for AWS S3. Required for MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, and other providers.
Enable path-style addressing. Required for MinIO. Leave disabled for AWS S3 and DigitalOcean Spaces.
AWS region (e.g. eu-central-1). For DigitalOcean Spaces use the slug like fra1.
AWS IAM secret access key, or the equivalent secret for your S3-compatible provider.
Optional AWS session token when using temporary credentials (e.g. from STS).
integrations.providers.storage_s3.descri: Store attachments and files in AWS S3, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO, or any S3-compatible object storage.
integrations.providers.storage_s3.title: S3-Compatible Storage
integrations.providers.sync_akeneo.crede: Use the base Akeneo PIM URL, without a trailing slash.
Create a connected app or API client in Akeneo and copy its client id.
Use the client secret generated for the Akeneo API connection.
Use the password for the dedicated Akeneo API user.
Create a dedicated Akeneo user for synchronization and grant only the product/catalog permissions it needs.
integrations.providers.sync_akeneo.descr: Import Akeneo product catalogs, family-driven attributes, and products into Helios with resilient batch sync.
